findings.claim: Acceptance requires sufficient supplied visibility into the actual worker audit-hook implementation to assess the goal.
findings.observed: The caller-declared diff visibility contract is incomplete and omits the actual audit package, actual worker pipeline/trigger implementation, and relevant tests; only unrelated documentation/environment files and a partial OpenAPI file are visible.
findings.rationale: The omitted paths contain the code and caller-level behavior that would prove or disprove wiring of real worker boundaries. Under the supplied visibility contract their absence is not implementation absence, but it prevents a trustworthy semantic verdict.
findings.required: Provide a complete task-scoped diff or equivalent caller-supplied implementation evidence covering the actual worker callers, composition/build seam, audit package changes, and relevant caller-level tests, then repeat acceptance review.

findings.claim: Because the manifest declares TDD required, the supplied proof must show an implementation-specific RED failure followed by GREEN on the same focused command.
findings.observed: The RED phase fails during test collection because the declared dependency pypdf is missing, before any task-specific assertion executes; the checkpoint explicitly states that this is an environment collection failure rather than assertion-level RED. The later run passes after dependency installation.
findings.rationale: A dependency/import failure does not establish that the new worker audit-hook requirement was first captured by a failing test, so the artifact does not prove the mandatory RED-to-GREEN implementation cycle.
findings.required: Supply valid TDD provenance showing a task-specific test assertion failing before the implementation and the same focused command passing after the implementation.

goals.summary: Monitoring MVP: napojení skutečných worker hranic na audit
